subject: Contract language: metering & streaming token rounding + tier mapping
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir@atlasai.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@atlasai.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Clarify how you meter streaming + discount tiers

Marcus —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Legal has one outstanding item before we sign: we need explicit contract language that defines exactly how "tokens" are metered for Hosted API usage, particularly for streaming responses and how rounding is applied. Our procurement partner is also mapping commit tiers to a clear monthly metering window. Two quick asks:

1) Can you provide a short, precise clause we can include in the SOW describing how streaming fragments aggregate into billable tokens and how fractional tokens are rounded?
2) We need a table that maps commit tiers to discount bands (monthly usage buckets) so Finance can validate total cost modeling.

We want to avoid ambiguity around per-request vs per-stream chunk accounting — small differences materially change our forecast. If you can send suggested language we can run it through our counsel.

Appreciate it,
Samir
AtlasAI
[attachment: procurement_summary.xlsx]
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T10:07:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Clarify how you meter streaming + discount tiers

Looping you both in — Samir from Atlas has a legal ask about meter definitions and commit->discount mapping. Notes:

- They want a clause for SOW that leaves no room for interpretation on streaming chunk aggregation and rounding.
- They also want a clear tier map we can put into the agreement (monthly buckets with effective % discount).

Draft idea below (very rough). Please propose firm wording and the table we can attach to the SOW. Also flag any risk if we commit to a specific rounding algorithm (billing systems must match).

DRAFT (internal):
"Metering and Rounding: For the Hosted API, Redwood measures metered usage in metered-tokens. For each API request, the metered-tokens equals the sum of prompt tokens and generated tokens exchanged for that request. For streaming responses that emit multiple fragments, the metered-tokens will be computed as the total tokens generated for the request, aggregated across all fragments. Any fractional token measurement resulting from internal instrumentation will be rounded up to the nearest whole token for billing purposes. Token usage will be reported on a per-request basis and totaled over the monthly metering window for purposes of applying commit thresholds and discounts."

I think we should avoid "per-chunk rounding" promises — stick to per-request aggregation then round up.

Marcus
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Clarify how you meter streaming + discount tiers

Agree with Marcus' direction. Suggested final clause and an accompanying tier mapping table below — clean, contractual, and implementable by billing:  

Proposed SOW Clause (concise):
"Metering and Billing. Redwood will meter usage in whole tokens (\"Metered Tokens\"). For each API request, Metered Tokens equals the sum of tokens in the request payload and the tokens generated by Redwood in response. For streaming responses, Metered Tokens are calculated by aggregating the total tokens generated for the request across all streaming fragments. Fractional tokens resulting from measurement will be rounded up to the nearest whole token. Metered Tokens are reported per calendar month (the \"Metering Period\"). Any committed threshold and corresponding discounts are applied based on total Metered Tokens consumed during the applicable Metering Period. Any shortfall against a committed monthly amount shall be invoiced at the then-applicable list price and any overages above committed amounts will be billed at the agreed overage rate."

Pricing Appendix (example mapping — edit numbers as needed):
- Tier A: Commit >= 0M and < 50M tokens / month -> 0% discount (list price)
- Tier B: Commit >= 50M and < 250M tokens / month -> 10% discount
- Tier C: Commit >= 250M and < 1B tokens / month -> 18% discount
- Tier D: Commit >= 1B tokens / month -> 25% discount + enterprise terms

Operational notes:
- Metering window = calendar month for simplicity with a monthly true-up (no daily carry).
- Streaming: we should confirm that SDK/ingest counts align with runtime instrumentation — Monica, can ops confirm the billing telemetry emits per-request totals?
- VAT / tax note: these discounts apply to charges pre-tax; Atlas needs to confirm local tax treatment.

If this looks good, Marcus can send to Samir with SOW and redline.

Lauren
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@atlasai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Legal Team <legal@atlasai.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T15:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Clarify how you meter streaming + discount tiers

Samir —

Thanks for the clear ask. Per our internal alignment (cc'd Lauren and Monica), please see a proposed SOW clause and a starter tier table attached. Key points summarized:

- Metering model: "Metered Tokens" = prompt tokens + generated tokens, aggregated on a per-request basis. For streaming, we aggregate across fragments and report the total generated tokens per request.
- Rounding: fractional measurements are rounded up to the next whole token for billing.
- Metering period: calendar month (monthly true-up).
- Tier table: example bands and associated discounts included in the attached Pricing Appendix.

Proposed contractual clause (copyable):
"Metering and Billing. Redwood will meter usage in whole tokens (\"Metered Tokens\"). For each API request, Metered Tokens equals the sum of tokens in the request payload and the tokens generated in response. For streaming responses, Metered Tokens are calculated by aggregating total tokens generated for the request across all streaming fragments. Fractional tokens resulting from measurement will be rounded up to the nearest whole token. Metered Tokens are reported per calendar month (the \"Metering Period\"), and any committed thresholds and corresponding discounts will be applied based on total Metered Tokens consumed during the Metering Period."

Attached: Redwood_SOW_v1.3.pdf (contains Pricing Appendix) and a redline contract for your counsel to review. If this matches what you need, I'll initiate DocuSign after you confirm the tier numbers.

Thanks —
Marcus
Redwood Inference
Business Development

From: Samir Shah <samir@atlasai.com>

Date: 2026-12-03T16:10:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Clarify how you meter streaming + discount tiers

Marcus —

Thanks, that language looks good and is exactly the clarity our legal team needed. A couple of follow-ups before we sign:

1) Can you confirm that the telemetry you bill from matches the per-request totals SDKs emit (Monica mentioned you'll validate)? We just want to avoid discrepancies between what our internal usage tracking shows and what your billing reports show.
2) On the tier numbers: Finance wants Tier B to start at 75M instead of 50M and Tier C at 300M — we can negotiate but please share any flexibility.
3) VAT: our tax team will apply local VAT as applicable; will Redwood provide tax invoices that separate pre-tax amount and tax?

If you can confirm (1) and (3) and acknowledge the tier counterproposal, we can route to signatures.

Samir
AtlasAI
